newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-PARMA COACH HITS OUT AT REFEREES.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PARMA COACH HITS OUT AT REFEREES.

text.p: Parma coach Carlo Ancelotti, shown a red card on Sunday in a 1-1 draw that effectively handed the Italian championship to Juventus, said on Monday that refereeing mistakes had cost his club dearly.

"It would be exaggerated to say that the championship has been dictated by refereeing decisions, Juventus deserved to win and a penalty more or a penalty less cannot undermine certain values," he said.
"Parma recognises certain qualities but we cannot stay silent in the face of decisions obvious to all."
Ancelotti said that Parma had suffered refereeing mistakes in their last two matches, when they suffered a late equalising penalty by AC Milan and then by Juventus on Sunday.

He said the dubious call against Milan meant that second-placed Parma faced Juventus with a six-point difference rather than four. "It would have been a different match. Yesterday the referee got it wrong," he said.
Juventus grabbed a first half equaliser on Sunday when Christian Vieri was judged to have been fouled. Ancelotti was shown the red card for protesting with his players.
Ancelotti said his biggest regret was Parma's shaky start to the season, when his job looked in danger and midfielder Gianfranco Zola left to join Chelsea in England.

He said he had not wanted Zola to leave and had intended to find a way to play him with Argentine striker Hernan Crespo and Italy's Enrico Chiesa. "We might have let in more goals, but we would have scored far more," he said.
